affected_boundaries: temporary upstream probe and fetched remote-tracking ref

observed_behavior: The recovery fixture returned UNCONFIRMED after restoring the temporary remote upstream probe and expecting a normal retry.
expected_behavior: Independent fixture cases restore all state created by the preceding probe, while production fetch remains non-forcing.
causal_mechanism: The divergence probe advanced both the bare remote branch and the shared local remote-tracking ref. Restoring only the remote branch left the tracking ref ahead; the explicit non-forcing fetch rejected its backward update.

anti_pattern.structural_description: Fixture cleanup restores the producer state but leaves its observed local projection changed.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: The subsequent case crosses a different ancestry boundary than its declared starting state.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Undo only the probe-created ref changes on both sides of the fixture boundary.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Preserve the upstream probe commit under its own ref and compare-and-swap restore both the disposable remote branch and its local tracking ref. Preserve production refusal of non-fast-forward fetch.

applicability_conditions: One disposable fixture runs sequential upstream-divergence and successful-retry cases.
known_non_matches: A genuine upstream history rewind remains an unresolved observation and must not be forced through by production recovery.
confirmation_evidence: The fixture failed with UNCONFIRMED immediately after its upstream restore.
A minimal Git-only probe reproduced fetch exit 1 with the non-fast-forward rejection after restoring just the remote branch.
Restoring both fixture-created ref changes makes all three focused PostgreSQL review/publication scenarios pass with zero failures or skips.
regression_proofs: tests/rolling-campaign-store.integration.test.ts: real PostgreSQL serializes allocation, retains ownership and persists accepted review
